name: Intuit Inc.
hidden_common_driver: US consumers and small businesses, and the same AI-substitution risk across all products
one_line_note: Credit Karma fell 10% in FY2023 while small business grew 24% and consumer tax 6%; segment revenue never grew less than 9%. The waves are small (2.9% average) and the segments share one customer type.

name: Raymond James Financial, Inc.
hidden_common_driver: Rates: the bank's NII and the private client group's cash-sweep fees both rise with rates; deals drive capital markets
one_line_note: Bank revenue rose 74% and 154% in 2022-23 while capital markets fell 3% and 29%, a real offset; but private client (60%+) and the bank both ride the same rate tailwind.

name: The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation
hidden_common_driver: Global asset levels and custody volumes feed every segment; the offset comes from rates (deposit NII up when asset values fall)
one_line_note: Securities services and market & wealth services rose 11% in 2022 while investment & wealth management fell 12%; segment revenue never fell after 2019, but the weak segment's profit went from $1.23B to $47M.

name: The Hartford Insurance Group, Inc.
hidden_common_driver: No single shared driver found: commercial P&C (pricing cycle), personal P&C (auto inflation), group benefits (employment and mortality), funds (market levels)
one_line_note: Personal insurance fell 6% a year in 2019-20 while business insurance grew 7-18%, and segment revenue never fell; segment net income fell 16% in the worst year. A genuine mix, small enough to stay simple.

name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
hidden_common_driver: US interest rates and the credit cycle: rates move consumer-bank NII and the 2020/2022 reserve builds and 2021 releases hit all three segments' profit together (segment profit changes correlate +0.64)
one_line_note: The model: consumer banking fell 7% in 2020 while CIB rose 21%, and CIB fell 4% in 2022 while consumer banking rose 10%, so segment revenue never fell; profit still swung with credit reserves. Alex already owns it.

name: Roper Technologies, Inc.
hidden_common_driver: Vertical software sold to niche markets; growth largely bought (Vertafore, Frontline, Procare, CentralReach)
one_line_note: Segment revenue never fell after the 2022 exit from industrial businesses; offsets are small and timing-driven.

name: Intercontinental Exchange, Inc.
hidden_common_driver: No single shared driver: exchanges ride volatility, fixed income & data are subscriptions, mortgage technology rides mortgage originations (rates); a rate shock helps the first and hurts the third
one_line_note: Mortgage technology fell 20% in 2022 while exchanges rose 9%, and total segment revenue never fell (worst +0.8%); but mortgage growth was bought (Ellie Mae 2020, Black Knight 2023), so only 2 clean mortgage years exist.

name: Bank of America Corporation
hidden_common_driver: Fed funds rate: net interest income sits inside consumer, wealth and global banking at once; the 2020 reserve build cut profit in three of four segments
one_line_note: Global Markets (+20% in 2020) offset a 14% consumer-banking fall, but total segment revenue still fell 4.9% and segment profit 36.5% in 2020; a rate-sensitive bank with one trading hedge.

name: Arch Capital Group Ltd.
hidden_common_driver: Insurance and reinsurance share the P&C pricing cycle (now 93% of premiums); mortgage insurance on US housing credit is the diversifier but has shrunk from 25% to 7% of premiums
one_line_note: Mortgage premiums fell 8-10% in 2021-22 while insurance and reinsurance grew 25-39%, a real offset in revenue; but underwriting income fell 56% in its worst year and the diversifier is fading.

name: Johnson & Johnson
hidden_common_driver: Pharma and medtech have different drivers (patents and launches vs elective procedures); consumer health was spun off in 2023
one_line_note: Medtech fell 12% in 2020 while pharma rose 8%, a real offset, and segment revenue never fell; but only two segments now, and pharma's patent cliffs (Stelara) are a single-stream risk.

name: Textron Inc.
hidden_common_driver: Business jets, helicopters, defense and auto parts have different drivers
one_line_note: Textron Aviation fell 23% and Industrial 21% in 2020 while Bell grew 2%; the weak segments were the big ones, so the total fell 14.5%.

name: PepsiCo, Inc.
hidden_common_driver: Consumer staples across regions; offsets are mostly currency and regional timing
one_line_note: Latin America fell 8% in 2020 while Asia rose 18%; segment revenue never fell, but the segments are one product family on different maps.

name: Moody's Corporation
hidden_common_driver: Two segments with different drivers (bond issuance vs subscriptions); the cyclical one is the bigger one
one_line_note: Ratings fell 28% in 2022 while analytics rose 15%: a real offset, but ratings were 62% of revenue so the total still fell 11.6% and profit 25%. The weak segment is the large one.

name: Citigroup Inc.
hidden_common_driver: Citi's own restructuring (exits, transformation spending) and rates; segment profit changes correlate +0.55
one_line_note: Services (+25% in 2022) offset a 31% fall in Banking, which is real offsetting, but segment profit fell 34% in 2022 and EPS has compounded only 7.7% a year; the offsets protect revenue, not earnings.

name: Abbott Laboratories
hidden_common_driver: No single shared driver across nutrition, diagnostics, devices and established pharma; COVID testing created the big wave
one_line_note: Diagnostics rose 40% and 45% in 2020-21 then fell 39% in 2023 while devices grew 14%; total fell 8% in 2023. The offsets are real but the wave came from one event.

name: MetLife, Inc.
hidden_common_driver: Interest rates and credit spreads on the general-account portfolio feed every segment's earnings
one_line_note: Retirement (pension risk transfer, lumpy) swung +64% and -19% while Latin America grew 17-22% a year; segment revenue fell 3.8% in 2023 and segment profit 20% in 2022. Real offsets, but a rate machine underneath.

name: McCormick & Company, Incorporated
hidden_common_driver: No single shared driver: consumer spices (home cooking) vs flavor solutions (food makers and restaurants)
one_line_note: Consumer rose 10% in 2020 while flavor solutions fell 3.5%; in 2022 consumer fell 4.6% while flavor rose 9%. Textbook offset, but small business, slow growth (EPS +1% a year).

name: RTX Corporation
hidden_common_driver: Commercial air traffic drives Collins and Pratt (two-thirds of revenue); defense budget drives Raytheon
one_line_note: Collins and Pratt fell 26% and 20% in 2020; Raytheon held, but it was too small to stop a 23% fall; Pratt's 2023 engine recall is company-specific.
